notes:
This is a handwritten mathematical page, numbered 2 at the bottom left, with no date or title. The displays are numbered (6), (7), and (8). The page is complete as supplied; the deleted final fragment Si X est de t.f. et is retained as a fragment, without adding a continuation. No other page was consulted.

The upper sequence has a clear cursive E with two rounded open lobes. The smaller left-hand sign of (8) has a reduced curled-hook/diagonal/lower-hook form. The clear E in (6) and the explicit description of (8) as its partial splitting support reading this second abbreviated sign as the same E; the isolated smaller form is less explicit. The roof-and-two-legs pi form is shared with other handwritten pi/Pi forms, so its fundamental-group role, also agreed by both witnesses here, supports lowercase pi without changing a distinct visible letter. The X forms consist of rounded crossed strokes. Their exact modern font family is not recoverable from this leaf alone, so C’s plain X convention is retained and H’s fraktur font is not entered as a separate substantive error. Q-bar in (7) has an internal retrace/doubled left stem; the interline Q is similarly retraced. Both denote the same written field Q. C’s bold Q convention is retained without claiming that a different field alphabet has been established merely by a font choice.

The vertical equality under pi_1(X), Aut(X-tilde/X), and the downward map from script G_X to Gamma in (6) are all preserved. H’s editorial note already describes these placements, so they are not treated as H omissions. The extra comma H places after the final 1 has no source ink. The crossed La donnée d’un point precedes the live Considérons un point. Immediately after that live phrase, the xi and additional right X-like cluster are reproduced graphically under one uncertainty wrapper. A low index and earlier overwritten writing remain possible; neither an explicit deletion nor an unqualified subscript is asserted.

In the NB, the interline condition begins X est de t.f. /Q-bar et and ends with a small sep-like abbreviation. A descending p-like component favors sep, but the abbreviated form remains uncertain. No accent or final period is supplied confidently. Its apparent grammatical connection to the following G_X est fini is preserved as written; no conjunction or punctuation has been added to improve the sentence. The line beneath the insertion bends down on the left to attach before the baseline G_X. Both witnesses place the added text there already; the graphic difference is the under-running line and descending curve. The author’s literal NB abbreviation, profini, s-groupe, and the three dots after ouvert are retained. The three dots and the closing parenthesis plus following period were visible in the native halves.

After On trouve alors, the source has si on choisit, not H’s dès qu’on choisit. The raised X-tilde(xi) is correctly located before pointé in both witnesses. Its curved descending leader, omitted in their renderings, is drawn. The source writes rev. universel and au dessus without an added hyphen.

In (8), the vertical sign is a tall open U/cup whose left arm is longer than its right arm. There is no separable arrowhead. The inclusion interpretation is compatible with the subgroup notation in the prose, but a directed hooked arrow is not substituted for the ink. The final horizontal segment toward 1 has a short downward terminal tick and no two-wing arrowhead. That tick is reproduced. The other horizontal arrow and the diagonal arrow from the stabilizer toward E_X have visible heads and keep their directions.

The final paragraph contains the negative ne. It reads hom. mod composition avec autom intérieurs: hom has a period, mod and autom do not; avec has no following un; autom remains abbreviated and intérieurs is plural. The terminal pi_1(X) and its period are retained. H’s uncertainty on qu’un is resolved by the readable letters without generating a certainty-only change row.

The mathematical check recorded here is conditional and local. Assuming the pointed lifting property of the universal covering object used in the manuscript, uniqueness of a lift fixing the chosen point gives a homomorphic section on the stabilizer, and replacing the chosen lift by a deck translate conjugates the section. This does not establish the existence and topological properties of all the groups on this leaf, nor the NB assertion about profiniteness and openness, whose definitions/hypotheses are not supplied in full here. No uncertain ink was repaired using that argument.

Each saved crop was made once from its recorded original-coordinate box, mildly autocontrasted, enlarged by LANCZOS to 3200 pixels on its longer side and sharpened slightly; no crop was rotated. Each of those six crops was personally viewed once. The main reader independently viewed the original/crops and supplied local adjudications, which are not counted as this reader’s views. No OCR, external research, compilation, other-page reading or global record write was performed.

check_events.statement: Under the pointed universal-cover lifting property, the stabilizer of xi admits a section of (6) after choosing a lift of xi; changing the chosen lift changes that section by conjugation by a deck transformation.
check_events.place: Paragraph introducing (8), diagram (8), and final paragraph
check_events.outcome: Let p:U→X have the pointed lifting property and choose u above xi. For each g fixing xi, let s_u(g) be the unique lift of g fixing u. The composite s_u(g)s_u(h) fixes u and lifts gh, so uniqueness gives s_u(gh)=s_u(g)s_u(h); projection back to the acting group gives g. If the chosen point is changed to ku for a deck transformation k, then k s_u(g) k^{-1} fixes ku and lifts g, so uniqueness gives s_{ku}(g)=k s_u(g) k^{-1}. This checks the section/conjugacy mechanism under the stated lifting assumptions, without proving those assumptions or the separate topological NB.
